problem: The existing Autotools flags include bare -Woverloaded-virtual, which GCC 13 treats as level 2. DRW_Entity has two virtual parseDwg overloads and many derived types intentionally override only one; GCC 13 reported the hidden overloads as errors under -Werror. Those methods and dispatch existed before this change.
compatibility_analysis: Adding protected using-declarations throughout the inheritance tree changes source lookup: a downstream subclass call parseDwg(version, buffer, 0) becomes ambiguous, an inherited Vertex four-argument zero call becomes ambiguous, and an inferred address of the previously single visible protected method becomes overloaded. A forwarding template cannot restore member-address source compatibility. The production change therefore leaves all headers, virtual dispatch, vtables and layouts untouched.
policy: Autoconf probes -Woverloaded-virtual=1 with -Werror. When accepted, Autotools selects level 1, which diagnoses complete hiding but intentionally does not diagnose partial-overload hiding; GCC bare -Woverloaded-virtual selected level 2, so this is a deliberate reduction in partial-override diagnostic coverage. When unsupported, the original bare flag remains. Full -Wall -Wextra -pedantic -Werror remains enabled; the pre-existing GCC parser-file -Wno-extra policy is unchanged. CMake warning flags are unchanged.

candidate_source.method: git archive HEAD at the above commit, then copy exactly the four named workspace candidate files. The standalone probe was added to source-release-files.am/txt in the isolated snapshot only; shared inventories are to be regenerated by the integrator. No other workspace changes were copied.
